messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: writing output CSV with headers
parts:
Stan's now set up to write a header file so that
the samples can easily be read into R or by another
CSV reader.

R can't read brackets, even with quotes, so I'm using
a period in place of a left bracket (see the example
coming up).

Stan now outputs all parameters, derived parameters
and generated quantities. (To stop printing, move
a derived param variable to a local model variable and a
generated quantity variable to a local variable in the
generated quantity block.)

For a very simple example of what you get,

stan/src/models/temp.stan
---------------------
parameters {
double y;
double z[2];
}
derived parameters {
double y_adj;

y_adj <- fabs(y);
}
model {
y ~ normal(0,1);
for (n in 1:2)
z[n] ~ normal(-10,5);
}
generated quantities {
double z_adj[2];

for (n in 1:2)
z_adj[n] <- z[n] * z[n];
}
-------------

Then variables are output in the order declared:

stan/samples.csv
---------------------------
y,z.1,z.2,y_adj,z_adj.1,z_adj.2
-0.34928,-1.73304,-16.7099,0.34928,3.00342,279.22
-1.02764,2.94466,-19.654,1.02764,8.671,386.282
1.1003,4.28888,-17.7973,1.1003,18.3945,316.743
-0.218579,3.60317,-18.0157,0.218579,12.9828,324.565
...
--------------------

This is just the output for a single chain.

I could read it into R as:

> stan.fit <- read.table('samples.csv', header=TRUE, sep=',')

Is there some kind of R magic I could use to reconstitute,
which would work like the following code:

> y[] = stan.fit$y
> z_adj = matrix(nrow=2000,ncol=2)
> z_adj[,1] = stan.fit$z.1
> z_adj[,2] = stan.fit$z.2

This would be enough to get a crude R2WinBUGS
toolchain going. It'd be better to do it all directly
in Rcpp. That'd be more like R2jags.

- Bob

On Jan 16, 2:49 am, Bob Carpenter <c...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> I could read it into R as:
>
>  > stan.fit <- read.table('samples.csv', header=TRUE, sep=',')
>
> Is there some kind of R magic I could use to reconstitute,
> which would work like the following code:
>
>  > y[] = stan.fit$y
>  > z_adj = matrix(nrow=2000,ncol=2)
>  > z_adj[,1] = stan.fit$z.1
>  > z_adj[,2] = stan.fit$z.2
>
> This would be enough to get a crude R2WinBUGS
> toolchain going.  It'd be better to do it all directly
> in Rcpp.  That'd be more like R2jags.

Here is such a function

df2matrices <-
function(X) {

cn <- colnames(X)
cn_grouped <- sapply(cn, function(x) strsplit(x, split = "\\.")
[[1]][1])
ucn_grouped <- unique(cn_grouped)
Z <- lapply(ucn_grouped, function(x) X[,names(which(cn_grouped ==
x))])
names(Z) <- ucn_grouped
return(Z)
}

In the case of src/models/bugs_examples/vol1/blocker , the R would be

post <- read.csv(file = "samples.csv", header = TRUE)
colnames(post)

[1] "d" "sigmasq_delta" "mu.1" "mu.2"
"mu.3" "mu.4" "mu.5"
[8] "mu.6" "mu.7" "mu.8" "mu.9"
"mu.10" "mu.11" "mu.12"
[15] "mu.13" "mu.14" "mu.15" "mu.16"
"mu.17" "mu.18" "mu.19"
[22] "mu.20" "mu.21" "mu.22" "delta.1"
"delta.2" "delta.3" "delta.4"
[29] "delta.5" "delta.6" "delta.7" "delta.8"
"delta.9" "delta.10" "delta.11"
[36] "delta.12" "delta.13" "delta.14" "delta.15"
"delta.16" "delta.17" "delta.18"
[43] "delta.19" "delta.20" "delta.21" "delta.22"
"sigma_delta"

Z <- df2matrices(post)
names(Z)

[1] "d" "sigmasq_delta" "mu" "delta"
"sigma_delta"

t(sapply(Z, dim))

[,1] [,2]
d 1000 1
sigmasq_delta 1000 1
mu 1000 22
delta 1000 22
sigma_delta 1000 1


However, I am not sure why one would want to do this. We have a lot of
post.R files under src/models/bugs_examples/ that analyzes the output
via the coda library, which (in the case of only 1 chain) is about as
easy as calling

library(coda)
MCMC <- as.mcmc(post)

If you wanted it to work with R2WinBUGS, then you would need to make a
parameters x chains x iterations array that is appropriate for
as.bugs.array().

In neither case would you want to first carve the mus and deltas into
their own matrices ...

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: writing output CSV with headers
parts:
help(as.mcmc, package = "coda")

will show you the documentation, but is basically just "pass it a
matrix or data.frame with columns as parameters".

If you use R2WinBUGS to *estimate* a model via WinBUGS, then they have
some parsing of the BUGS output into what is called a bugs.array that
has 3 dimensions for parameters, chains, and draws. But, if you are
not using WinBUGS, then you have to construct your own bugs.array to
analyze it with Andrew's plotting functions in the R2WinBUGS package.

Andrew would probably want a function that takes Stan output from
multiple chains and makes it into a bugs.array, but I think most
people would prefer to use the coda package.

In both cases, we can supplement these objects with information on the
burnin, thinning rate, etc., which isn't knowable from samples.csv,
but should be easy when calling from rstan.

Ben
